fieldCases.setting: Windows 11, Windows PowerShell 5.1, run in the Shelra repository

realiza una amplia auditoria al proyecto de shelra pero quiero que sean algo amplio, genera un plan de investigacion profunda, analisis validacion del mercado
tienes que buscar en google contexto

tambien debes revisar todo el codigo actual

shelra.result: Wrote docs/AUDIT-2026-09-23.md (348 lines). Of about 106 claims a check found 38% true (the module inventory), 22% stale, 16% false (its OpenRouter ranking among them) and 17% misleading; see docs/verification/AUDIT-2026-09-23-review.md. It read four files of 50,000-200,000 characters whole (7.4M input tokens in one round), the stream stalled three times, and the completion gate twice refused its re-reading of the report as verification. The owner approved the live run as passing the same day, before the check.

fixes.what: read_file returned whole files; a read now stops at 2,000 lines and 50,000 characters and says where to read on.
The completion gate asked three times for a check that no document can have; a turn that only wrote documents is now asked once to check its facts, then reported unverified.
Headless JSON output dropped the gate's closing note and the retry and model-switch notices.
Every step re-sent every earlier tool result; past 160,000 characters, results older than the last three steps go out as a one-line note.
A check piped into head counted as passing, and a type-check counted as proof of an audit document.
Acceptance criteria sent as a JSON array inside a string became one criterion holding the whole array.
A round cut short by a stall was saved with 0 tokens, so spend limits missed it.
AGENTS.md sent agents to docs/architecture/, most of it history about an older codebase; its file names ended up in the audits.
The re-run's clone had no dependencies installed, so every check the model ran failed.

reruns.result: Three drafts of the report (the last 525 lines) and six "verification" text files. The largest read fell from 201,000 characters to 50,000 and read_file returned 240,000 in all (672,000 before), yet input stayed near 8.9M tokens: more steps, and three gate rounds it answered by echoing "VERIFIED" and writing those files. Nemotron stalled twice and was overloaded once; the run ended on openrouter/free. Its line counts and module paths check out; its counts of files (166, not 331) and tests ("332 passing"; nothing ran), its two market sizes that disagree and "memory unique among terminal agents" do not.

Seven research documents. Nemotron was overloaded and the run moved to openrouter/free, then stalled six times (the owner was using the same free quota): 40 minutes. The single fact-check request did what it asks: the model grepped about twenty claims and corrected two numbers, in its answer but not in the files. But it checked quotes, not meaning: "the model catalog is empty" (primeCatalog fills it at startup, as the comment above says), "128K context for every cloud model" (a fallback) and "zero retries" (the harness retries rounds itself) came back confirmed. A type-check piped into head counted as a pass, so the turn ended without the [Not verified] note. Recorded input about 5.2M tokens; rounds cut short record none.

One report, 110 lines, from only 8 files read (23-30 in the other runs). Its first draft named four files that do not exist (loop.ts, control-plane.ts, ollama.ts, http.ts), taken from docs about the older ShelraCode/ codebase; the fact-check request found them and the model rewrote the file. Still wrong: "local-first, no cloud by default", "the CLI entry is src/cli/installation.ts". Its piped checks no longer counted and the turn ended "[Not verified — 1 document(s) written ...]", yet the answer said the type-check "passes with 3 warnings" over TS7006 errors (the clone had no dependencies). 32K recorded input tokens a step (92-120K before); replaying its steps without clearing gives about 3.7M in all, against 1.76M recorded (two cut rounds uncounted).
